title: Refactor Go items handler from global state to Server struct
description: A Go HTTP items handler uses package-level global variables and standalone functions. Refactor to a Server struct with an injected store and receiver methods, preserving all behaviour.

task_spec.prompt:
The items handler in internal/items/handler.go uses package-level global variables (store, nextID, mu) and standalone handler functions (ListItems, CreateItem, GetItem). Refactor it:

1. Define a Store interface with methods Set(item Item), GetByID(id int) (Item, bool), List() []Item, and Reset().

2. Create an InMemoryStore struct that implements Store using the same sync.Mutex + slice logic, but as receiver methods instead of globals.

3. Create a Server struct with a Store field and a constructor func NewServer(s Store) *Server.

4. Move ListItems, CreateItem, GetItem to receiver methods on *Server (func (srv *Server) ListItems(w, r), etc.).

5. Remove all package-level global variables. The package should now be side-effect free at import time.

6. Update the test file to construct a Server via NewServer(NewInMemoryStore()) instead of calling ResetStore(). All four existing tests must continue to pass.

Run go test ./... to confirm. Run go vet ./... to confirm no issues.
required_artifacts: All 4 existing tests pass with updated test setup
success_criteria: Global state eliminated — tests create their own Server instances
Interface enables future test injection of a mock store
Behaviour unchanged: same HTTP status codes and response shapes
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` to confirm no regressions from your refactor. Also review the code you changed — any remaining duplication, long functions, or unclear names to clean up?
Final pass: run `go test ./...` and confirm everything is green. Give me a one-line summary of what changed.
